As a long-time, if not particularly prolific, contributor the [Omnificent English Dictionary in Limerick Form](http://www.oedilf.com), I tend to think in terms of limericks when I'm stuck on writing projects. Likewise, I've said before that the kind of close reading required for writing detailed reviews is not, for me, sustainable for more than one such review a month. In that spirit, here are some limerick reviews of books I've read recently:

***The Left Hand of Darkness*** **by Ursula K LeGuin\
**There once was a person from Gethen\
Whose androgyny Gen' found distrethin'.\
Their romance felt forced,\
But I still endorse\
The pretend anthropology lethon.

***Far from Home*** **by Walter Tevis\
**I don't normally pay mind to Freud.\
Such readings I tend to avoid.\
But for this, there's no other:\
He's *down bad* for his mother.\
And he's screaming it into the void.\
\
***The Man Who Fell to Earth*** **by Walter Tevis\
**To me, all of Walter's books seem\
To have booze as their centermost theme.\
So too in this tale\
Of an alien fail:\
He got drunk, and gave up on his dream.

I could probably keep going, but let's [stick to three](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J8lRKCw2_Pk) so I don't set a bad precedent. I'll probably come back to this well fairly often. If you want to complain in the comments, please do so in the form of a limerick.
